base64.seoContent: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that represents binary data in an ASCII string format. It's commonly used for encoding data in URLs, emails, HTML, and APIs. This online Base64 encoder and decoder supports full UTF-8, handles Base64 padding (the trailing = characters), and works entirely in your browser. Whether you need to base64 encode a file, decode an API response, or convert data for URL-safe transport, this tool handles it instantly.

faqs.q: What is Base64 encoding?
faqs.a: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that converts binary data into ASCII characters. It's commonly used to transmit data safely over text-based protocols like HTTP and email.

faqs.q: Is Base64 encoding the same as encryption?
faqs.a: No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not encryption. Anyone can decode Base64 data. It's meant for data transport, not security.

faqs.q: Does this tool support UTF-8?
faqs.a: Yes. This tool fully supports UTF-8 encoding and decoding, allowing you to work with international characters and emojis.

faqs.q: How do I use openssl to base64 decode on the command line?
faqs.a: Run 'echo <base64string> | openssl base64 -d' to decode. To encode, use 'echo -n "text" | openssl base64'. The openssl base64 command is available on macOS and Linux by default.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Base64 and Base64URL?
faqs.a: Standard Base64 uses + and / as special characters, while Base64URL replaces them with - and _ to be safe in URLs and filenames. Base64URL also omits padding (=) characters.

faqs.q: What is Base64 padding and why are there = signs?
faqs.a: Base64 encodes 3 bytes into 4 characters. When the input length isn't a multiple of 3, padding characters (=) are added to make the output length a multiple of 4. One = means 2 bytes were encoded in the last group, == means 1 byte.

faqs.q: Can I Base64 encode a file?
faqs.a: Yes. On the command line use 'base64 < file.bin > file.b64' or 'openssl base64 -in file.bin'. For images, use our Image Base64 Converter tool which supports drag-and-drop file encoding.

faqs.q: Is it safe to use Base64 in URLs?
faqs.a: Standard Base64 is not URL-safe because + and / have special meanings in URLs. Use Base64URL encoding instead, which replaces + with - and / with _ . Most programming languages have built-in Base64URL functions.

faqs.q: What is URL encoding?
faqs.a: URL encoding replaces unsafe ASCII characters with a '%' followed by two hex digits. This ensures special characters are safely transmitted in URLs.

faqs.q: What's the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
faqs.a: encodeURI encodes a full URL but preserves characters like :, /, ?, &. encodeURIComponent encodes everything including those characters, making it suitable for query parameter values.

faqs.q: When should I URL encode?
faqs.a: Always URL encode when passing user input as query parameters, form data, or any URL component that may contain special characters like spaces, &, =, or #.

hash-generator.seoContent: Cryptographic hash functions generate a fixed-size hash value from input data. This online MD5 hash generator and SHA256 hash tool computes MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 hashes instantly in your browser. Hash functions are one-way: you cannot reverse a hash back to the original data. They're used for data integrity verification, password storage, digital signatures, file checksums, and deduplication. SHA-256 is recommended for security-sensitive applications, while MD5 remains useful for quick checksums despite being cryptographically broken.

faqs.q: What is a hash function?
faqs.a: A hash function takes input data and produces a fixed-size string of characters (hash). The same input always produces the same hash, but you cannot reverse a hash back to the original data.

faqs.q: Which hash algorithm should I use?
faqs.a: SHA-256 is recommended for most purposes. SHA-512 offers more security. MD5 and SHA-1 are considered weak for security but are still used for checksums.

faqs.q: Is my data safe?
faqs.a: Yes. All hash computation happens in your browser using the Web Crypto API. No data is sent to any server.

faqs.q: What is the difference between MD5 and SHA-256?
faqs.a: MD5 produces a 128-bit (32 hex character) hash and is fast but cryptographically broken — collisions can be generated. SHA-256 produces a 256-bit (64 hex character) hash and is considered secure. Use SHA-256 for security, MD5 only for non-security checksums.

faqs.q: What is a hash collision?
faqs.a: A hash collision occurs when two different inputs produce the same hash output. MD5 and SHA-1 have known collision vulnerabilities. SHA-256 and SHA-512 have no known practical collisions and are considered collision-resistant.

faqs.q: What is a hash salt and why is it important?
faqs.a: A salt is random data added to the input before hashing, making each hash unique even for identical inputs. Salting prevents rainbow table attacks on password hashes. Always use a unique salt per password when storing hashed passwords.

faqs.q: When should I use bcrypt instead of SHA-256 for passwords?
faqs.a: Always use bcrypt (or Argon2, scrypt) for password hashing. SHA-256 is too fast, making brute-force attacks feasible. Bcrypt is intentionally slow and includes built-in salting, making it far more secure for password storage.

faqs.q: Can I reverse a hash back to the original text?
faqs.a: No. Hash functions are one-way by design. You cannot mathematically reverse a hash. Attackers use brute-force or rainbow tables to find inputs that match a hash, which is why strong passwords and salting are essential.

Copy any hash value with the copy button

cron-parser.seoContent: Cron is a time-based job scheduler in Unix-like systems. A cron expression consists of 5 fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week. Use this cron schedule generator for CI/CD pipelines, crontab debugging, automated backups, and recurring task planning.

faqs.q: What is a cron expression?
faqs.a: A cron expression is a string of 5 fields (minute, hour, day, month, weekday) that defines a schedule for recurring tasks in Unix-like systems.

faqs.q: What do the special characters mean?
faqs.a: * means any value, / means step (*/5 = every 5), , means list (1,3,5), - means range (1-5), and specific numbers mean exact values.

faqs.q: Can I see when my cron job will run next?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your cron expression and the tool will show the next scheduled execution times, plus a human-readable description.

faqs.q: What are the 5 fields in a cron expression?
faqs.a: The 5 fields are: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12), and day of week (0-6, where 0 is Sunday). Each field can use numbers, wildcards (*), ranges (-), lists (,), and steps (/).

faqs.q: What is the difference between cron and crontab?
faqs.a: Cron is the daemon (background service) that runs scheduled tasks. Crontab (cron table) is the file where you define your cron jobs and their schedules. You edit the crontab using the 'crontab -e' command.

faqs.q: What are common cron expressions for everyday tasks?
faqs.a: Every 5 minutes: */5 * * * *. Daily at midnight: 0 0 * * *. Every Monday at 9am: 0 9 * * 1. Every hour: 0 * * * *. First day of every month: 0 0 1 * *. Weekdays at 8am: 0 8 * * 1-5.

faqs.q: How does cron handle timezones?
faqs.a: Standard Unix cron uses the system's local timezone. There is no timezone field in a cron expression. To run jobs in a specific timezone, set the TZ variable in your crontab or use tools that support timezone-aware scheduling.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Spring cron and Unix cron?
faqs.a: Spring cron expressions have 6 fields (adding seconds as the first field), while Unix cron has 5 fields. Spring cron also uses different syntax for day-of-week (1-7 where 1=Monday) compared to Unix (0-6 where 0=Sunday).

faqs.q: What does a 502 Bad Gateway error mean?

faqs.q: What is CIDR notation?
faqs.a: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) notation like /24 indicates how many bits are used for the network portion of an IP address. /24 means 24 network bits and 8 host bits, allowing 254 usable hosts.

faqs.q: How do I calculate the number of hosts in a subnet?
faqs.a: The formula is 2^(32-prefix) - 2 for IPv4. The subtraction accounts for the network address and broadcast address. A /24 subnet has 2^8 - 2 = 254 usable hosts.

faqs.q: What is the difference between network and broadcast address?
faqs.a: The network address is the first address in a subnet (all host bits 0) and identifies the subnet. The broadcast address is the last (all host bits 1) and sends packets to all hosts in the subnet.

hmac-generator.seoContent: HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) combines a cryptographic hash function with a secret key to verify both data integrity and authenticity. Unlike simple hashing, HMAC requires the secret key to generate and verify signatures, making it resistant to tampering. HMAC-SHA256 is the most commonly used variant and is required by many APIs and webhook systems (Stripe, GitHub, Shopify). This tool generates HMAC signatures using SHA-1, SHA-256, or SHA-512 algorithms. Enter your message and secret key, and get the signature in hexadecimal or Base64 format. All computation happens locally.

faqs.q: What is the difference between HMAC and a regular hash?
faqs.a: A regular hash (like SHA-256) only takes a message as input. HMAC also requires a secret key, so only parties who know the key can generate or verify the signature. This prevents tampering.

faqs.q: Which HMAC algorithm should I use?
faqs.a: HMAC-SHA256 is the most common and recommended choice. It offers strong security and is required by most modern APIs. Use SHA-1 only for legacy compatibility.

faqs.q: How do I verify a webhook signature with HMAC?
faqs.a: Compute the HMAC of the webhook payload using your secret key, then compare it to the signature in the webhook header. If they match, the webhook is authentic and untampered.

faqs.q: What cost factor should I use for bcrypt?

faqs.a: Yes. SHA-256 is designed to be fast, which makes it vulnerable to brute-force attacks. Bcrypt is intentionally slow and includes a built-in salt, making it much more secure for password storage.

faqs.q: Can I verify a password against a bcrypt hash?

faqs.q: What is a Go struct?
faqs.a: A struct in Go is a composite data type that groups variables together. Unlike maps, structs provide type safety — each field has a specific name and type. They're essential for unmarshaling JSON data.

faqs.q: What does 'PascalCase' field naming mean?
faqs.a: PascalCase (CapitalizedWords) is the Go convention for exported struct fields. The tool converts snake_case and kebab-case to PascalCase automatically for idiomatic Go code.

faqs.q: What are JSON struct tags used for?
faqs.a: JSON struct tags (e.g., `json:"field_name"`) tell Go's encoding/json package how to map between JSON keys and struct fields. Without them, field names must match exactly.

faqs.q: When should I use omitempty?
faqs.a: Use omitempty for optional fields. It tells Go to omit the field from JSON output if it has a zero value (nil, empty string, 0, false), making your JSON more compact.

faqs.q: How are nested objects handled?
faqs.a: Nested JSON objects become separate Go struct types with descriptive names. For example, a 'user' object inside 'profile' becomes struct type 'User', referenced in the parent struct.

json-to-zod.seoContent: Zod is a TypeScript-first schema validation library that lets you define schemas and validate data at runtime. When building TypeScript applications, Zod schemas provide both runtime validation and compile-time type inference. This tool analyzes your JSON data and generates corresponding Zod schemas with proper type mappings: strings become z.string(), numbers become z.number(), booleans become z.boolean(), arrays become z.array(), and nested objects become z.object(). The generated schemas can be used directly in your TypeScript project for form validation, API response validation, and more. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What is Zod?
faqs.a: Zod is a TypeScript-first schema declaration and validation library. It lets you define the shape of data and validates it at runtime while providing automatic TypeScript type inference.

faqs.q: How does JSON to Zod conversion work?

faqs.q: Can I use the output directly in my project?

faqs.q: Does it handle nested objects?
faqs.a: Yes. Nested objects are converted to nested z.object() calls with all their properties properly typed.

json-to-json-schema.seoContent: JSON Schema is a vocabulary for annotating and validating JSON documents. It's widely used for API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger), form generation, configuration validation, and data interchange. This tool analyzes your JSON data and generates a JSON Schema (draft-07) that describes its structure. It correctly identifies types, marks all existing fields as required, handles arrays with item schemas, and creates nested schemas for objects. The output can be used with any JSON Schema validator or integrated into OpenAPI specifications. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: What JSON Schema draft is used?
faqs.a: The tool generates schemas following JSON Schema draft-07, which is widely supported by validators and tools.

faqs.q: Are all fields marked as required?

faqs.q: Does it handle nested objects?
faqs.a: Yes. Nested objects generate nested schema definitions with their own properties and required arrays.

faqs.q: Can I use this with OpenAPI/Swagger?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated JSON Schema is compatible with OpenAPI specifications. You can paste the schema into your API documentation.

faqs.q: How do I create JSON Schema from JSON?
faqs.a: Paste your sample JSON data into the input panel and click Convert. The tool automatically detects types (string, number, boolean, array, object), marks all fields as required, and generates a complete JSON Schema definition.

faqs.q: What is JSON Schema used for?
faqs.a: JSON Schema defines the structure and validation rules for JSON data. It's used for API request/response validation, form generation, configuration file validation, and data documentation in OpenAPI/Swagger specs.

faqs.q: Does it support arrays of objects?
faqs.a: Yes. Arrays containing objects generate an 'items' schema with the object's properties defined. Mixed-type arrays use 'anyOf' to describe all possible item types.

css-to-js.seoContent: CSS-in-JS is a popular approach in modern frontend development, especially with React. Libraries like styled-components, Emotion, and React's inline styles use JavaScript objects instead of CSS strings. Converting CSS to JS objects requires changing property names from kebab-case to camelCase (font-size becomes fontSize), wrapping string values in quotes, and converting pixel values to numbers where appropriate. This tool automates the conversion process, handling selectors, property names, and values. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How are CSS property names converted?
faqs.a: Kebab-case CSS properties are converted to camelCase: font-size becomes fontSize, background-color becomes backgroundColor, border-radius becomes borderRadius.

faqs.q: Are pixel values converted to numbers?
faqs.a: Yes. Pure pixel values like 16px become the number 16. Values with other units (em, rem, %) remain as strings.

faqs.q: Does it handle CSS selectors?
faqs.a: Yes. CSS rules with selectors are converted to named JavaScript objects. Class selectors like .container produce a const named container.

faqs.q: Can I use the output with React?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated objects work with React's style prop, styled-components, Emotion, and other CSS-in-JS libraries.

faqs.q: What GraphQL types are supported?
faqs.a: The tool supports type, input, enum, scalar, and union definitions. It handles both nullable and non-null (!) types, and list types ([Type]).

faqs.q: Does it handle enums?

faqs.q: How is nullability handled?
faqs.a: Non-null types (!) become required TypeScript fields. Nullable types (without !) become optional fields with the ? suffix.

json-to-rust.seoContent: Rust's type system requires defining structs before deserializing JSON data with serde. Manually writing Rust structs for complex JSON APIs is time-consuming. This tool analyzes your JSON and generates Rust struct definitions with proper types (String, i64, f64, bool, Vec<T>), serde derive macros (Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone), and automatic snake_case field naming with #[serde(rename)] attributes when needed. Nested objects become separate named structs, and null values are wrapped in Option<T>. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to Rust structs?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON, set the root struct name, select derive macros, and click Convert. The tool generates Rust structs with proper types and serde attributes.

faqs.q: What derive macros are available?
faqs.a: You can toggle Debug, Clone, Serialize, and Deserialize. The serde import is added automatically when Serialize or Deserialize is selected.

faqs.q: How are field names handled?

faqs.q: How are null values handled?
faqs.a: Fields with null values are typed as Option<String>. This allows the field to be None when the value is null in JSON.

xml-to-json.pageDescription: Free XML to JSON converter online. Transform XML documents to JSON with attribute handling, nested elements, and array detection. Fast, instant, no signup.
xml-to-json.seoContent: XML and JSON are two of the most common data interchange formats. While XML uses tags and attributes, JSON uses key-value pairs and arrays. Converting XML to JSON is useful when migrating legacy systems, consuming SOAP APIs, or processing XML feeds in modern JavaScript applications. This tool parses XML and converts it to a structured JSON representation where elements become objects, attributes are prefixed with @, text content is stored as #text, and repeated elements automatically become arrays. It handles CDATA sections, self-closing tags, and nested structures. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: How are XML attributes handled?
faqs.a: Attributes are prefixed with @ in the JSON output. For example, <item id="1"> becomes {"@id": "1"}.

faqs.q: How is text content represented?
faqs.a: Text content within elements is stored as #text. If an element has both attributes and text, both are preserved: {"@attr": "val", "#text": "content"}.

faqs.q: Does it handle repeated elements?
faqs.a: Yes. When multiple sibling elements share the same tag name, they are automatically grouped into a JSON array.

faqs.q: Does it support CDATA sections?
faqs.a: Yes. CDATA sections are parsed and their content is included as text in the JSON output.

This favicon generator creates ICO and PNG favicons from text or emoji with customizable colors, sizes, and border radius. faqs.a: PNG is widely supported. ICO can contain multiple sizes.

faqs.q: Can I use emoji?
faqs.a: Yes! Modern browsers support emoji favicons with custom backgrounds.

faqs.q: What is the minimal valid ICO file format?
faqs.a: A minimal valid ICO file contains a 6-byte header (magic bytes, type, image count), a 16-byte directory entry (size, color info, data offset), and the image data. The smallest practical favicon is a 16x16 pixel ICO file, typically a few hundred bytes.

faqs.q: Should I use ICO, PNG, or SVG for my favicon?
faqs.a: ICO is the traditional format that supports multiple sizes in one file. PNG is widely supported and simpler. SVG favicons are the newest option, supported in modern browsers, and scale perfectly to any size. Use ICO for maximum compatibility.

faqs.q: How do I add a favicon to my website using Base64?
faqs.a: Add this to your HTML <head>: <link rel="icon" href="data:image/png;base64,...">. This embeds the favicon directly in your HTML without needing a separate file. This tool generates the Base64 data URI ready to use.

faqs.q: What favicon sizes should I include for PWA manifest?
faqs.a: For Progressive Web Apps, include 192x192 and 512x512 PNG icons in your manifest.json. Also include 16x16, 32x32, and 180x180 (Apple Touch) for complete browser and device coverage.

faqs.q: Why isn't my favicon showing up?
faqs.a: Common issues: browser cache (try hard refresh with Ctrl+Shift+R), wrong file path in the <link> tag, incorrect MIME type, or the ICO file is malformed. Place favicon.ico in your site root as a fallback, since browsers check there by default.

cron-expression-generator.faq3q: How do I run a job every 5 minutes?

faqs.q: How do I convert an image to Base64 online?
faqs.a: Upload or drag-and-drop your image file (PNG, JPG, SVG, GIF, WebP). The tool instantly generates the Base64 string, data URI, CSS background-image code, and HTML img tag — all without uploading to any server.

faqs.q: What is a Base64 data URI for images?
faqs.a: A data URI embeds image data directly in HTML or CSS using the format data:image/png;base64,... This eliminates an extra HTTP request but increases HTML size by ~33%. Best for small icons under 10KB.

faqs.q: Should I use Base64 images in production?
faqs.a: For small images (under 5-10KB like icons), Base64 data URIs reduce HTTP requests and can improve performance. For larger images, use regular file references — Base64 adds 33% size overhead and prevents browser caching.

faqs.q: How do I convert Base64 back to an image?
faqs.a: Paste the Base64 string (with or without the data:image/... prefix) into the decoder. The tool reconstructs the original image file which you can preview and download.

faqs.q: What image formats support Base64 encoding?
faqs.a: All image formats can be Base64-encoded: PNG, JPEG, GIF, SVG, WebP, ICO, BMP, and TIFF. The MIME type in the data URI (e.g., image/png) tells the browser how to interpret the data.

faqs.q: How do I decode a JWT token online?
faqs.a: Paste your JWT token into the input field. The decoder instantly splits it into header, payload, and signature sections, showing all claims including expiration time, issuer, and custom data.

faqs.q: Is it safe to decode JWT tokens in an online tool?
faqs.a: Yes, when the tool processes data entirely in your browser. DevToolBox never sends your JWT to any server — all decoding happens client-side using JavaScript.

faqs.q: What information is inside a JWT token?
faqs.a: A JWT contains three parts: the header (algorithm and type), the payload (claims like user ID, roles, expiration), and the signature (verification hash). The header and payload are Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted.

faqs.q: Can I verify a JWT signature online?
faqs.a: You can decode and inspect JWT tokens without the secret key. However, signature verification requires the signing key (for HMAC) or public key (for RSA/ECDSA), which should never be shared in online tools.

faqs.q: Why does my JWT show as expired?
faqs.a: The 'exp' claim in the payload is a Unix timestamp. If the current time exceeds this value, the token is expired. Check the decoded expiration date and compare it with the current UTC time.

faqs.q: How do I use capture groups in regex?
faqs.a: Wrap parts of your pattern in parentheses to create capture groups. Use (?:...) for non-capturing groups and (?<name>...) for named groups. The tester shows each group's match separately.

faqs.q: What does the g, i, m flag mean in regex?
faqs.a: g (global) finds all matches, i (case-insensitive) ignores letter case, m (multiline) makes ^ and $ match line starts/ends instead of string starts/ends. s (dotAll) makes . match newlines.

faqs.q: Why is my regex not matching?
faqs.a: Common issues: forgetting to escape special characters (. * + ? etc.), missing flags (especially g for multiple matches), or using syntax from a different regex flavor. Try simplifying your pattern and testing piece by piece.

faqs.q: What are HTML entities?
faqs.a: HTML entities are special codes that represent characters which have special meaning in HTML (like < > & ") or characters that cannot be typed on a standard keyboard. They start with & and end with ; (e.g., & for &, < for <).

faqs.q: Why do I need to encode HTML entities?
faqs.a: Encoding prevents XSS (cross-site scripting) attacks and ensures special characters display correctly. Without encoding, characters like < and > are interpreted as HTML tags, potentially breaking your page or creating security vulnerabilities.

faqs.q: What is the difference between named and numeric entities?
faqs.a: Named entities use descriptive names (e.g., & < ©). Numeric entities use character codes (e.g., & < ©). Named entities are more readable but not all characters have names. Numeric entities work for any Unicode character.

faqs.q: When should I use HTML entities vs UTF-8?
faqs.a: With UTF-8 encoding (recommended for all modern websites), you only need to encode &, <, >, and " in HTML context. Special characters like accented letters can be typed directly. Use entities only for these 4 HTML-special characters and for invisible characters.

faqs.q: How does IP address lookup work?
faqs.a: IP lookup queries geolocation databases that map IP address ranges to physical locations. These databases are compiled from ISP registrations, routing data, and other sources. Accuracy varies: country is 95-99% accurate, city is 50-80% accurate.

faqs.q: Is IP geolocation always accurate?
faqs.a: No. IP geolocation is approximate. It is accurate for country (95-99%) but less so for city (50-80%). VPN users, mobile networks, and corporate proxies can show incorrect locations. Never rely on IP location for critical decisions.

faqs.q: Can I find someone's exact address from their IP?
faqs.a: No. IP addresses do not reveal exact addresses. At best, you can determine the city or region. Only the Internet Service Provider (ISP) can map an IP to a specific subscriber, and they only share this with law enforcement via legal process.

faqs.a: Approximate geographic location (country, region, city), ISP name, organization name, timezone, AS number, and whether it is a known VPN/proxy/Tor exit node. You cannot get personal information like name or street address.

faqs.q: How many people are color blind?
faqs.a: Approximately 8% of men and 0.5% of women have some form of color vision deficiency. The most common type is red-green color blindness (deuteranopia/protanopia), affecting about 6% of men. This means roughly 1 in 12 male users.

faqs.q: How do I design for colorblind users?
faqs.a: Never rely solely on color to convey information. Use patterns, labels, icons, or underlines alongside color. Ensure sufficient contrast ratios (WCAG AA: 4.5:1). Test with simulation tools. Avoid problematic pairs like red/green or blue/purple.

faqs.q: What are the types of color blindness?
faqs.a: Protanopia (no red cones), deuteranopia (no green cones), tritanopia (no blue cones), and achromatopsia (total color blindness). Red-green deficiency (protanopia + deuteranopia) is by far the most common, affecting ~6% of males.

faqs.q: How do I read a cron expression?
faqs.a: A cron expression has 5 fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12), day of week (0-7). For example, '30 9 * * 1-5' means 'At 9:30 AM, Monday through Friday'.

faqs.q: What does */5 mean in cron?
faqs.a: The */5 syntax means 'every 5th unit'. In the minute field, */5 means every 5 minutes (0, 5, 10, 15...). In the hour field, */2 means every 2 hours. It is called a step value.

faqs.q: What is the difference between * and ? in cron?
faqs.a: The asterisk (*) means 'every value'. The question mark (?) is used in some cron implementations (like Quartz) for day-of-month or day-of-week to mean 'no specific value'. Standard cron uses * for both.

faqs.q: How do I schedule a job for the first Monday of every month?
faqs.a: Standard cron cannot directly express this. Use '0 0 1-7 * 1' (runs on Monday when the date is 1-7) or implement the logic in your script to check if today is the first Monday.

faqs.a: Flexbox is a CSS layout module that makes it easy to align and distribute space among items in a container.

faqs.q: When should I use flexbox?
faqs.a: Use flexbox for one-dimensional layouts (row OR column). For two-dimensional layouts, consider CSS Grid.

faqs.q: How do I center with flexbox?
faqs.a: Set display: flex, justify-content: center (horizontal), and align-items: center (vertical) on the container.

saml-decoder.seoContent: SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an XML-based framework for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity providers and service providers. SAML responses and requests are typically Base64-encoded. This tool decodes SAML tokens and formats the XML for easy reading. It supports both SAML Response (Base64 only) and SAML Request (Base64 + Deflate compression).

Copy the decoded XML for debugging or documentation

Verifying identity provider (IdP) configuration during SAML integration setup
Inspecting SAML NameID, audience restrictions, and conditions in authentication responses
Troubleshooting SAML signature validation errors between IdP and SP
Auditing SAML attribute mappings for user provisioning workflows

faqs.q: What is a SAML assertion and how do I decode it?
faqs.a: A SAML assertion is an XML document issued by an identity provider (IdP) that contains authentication and authorization statements about a user. Assertions are Base64-encoded for transport. Paste the encoded string into this tool to instantly decode it to readable XML.

faqs.q: How do I decode a SAML response from my browser?
faqs.a: Open your browser's developer tools (F12), go to the Network tab, and look for the POST request to your SP's ACS URL. The SAMLResponse parameter in the form data is the Base64-encoded response. Copy and paste it into this tool.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SAML and OAuth?
faqs.a: SAML is an XML-based protocol primarily used for enterprise SSO between identity providers and service providers. OAuth 2.0 is a JSON-based authorization framework used for API access and third-party app authorization. SAML handles authentication while OAuth focuses on authorization.

faqs.q: Can this tool decode Base64-encoded SAML with Deflate compression?
faqs.a: Yes. SAML Requests typically use Base64 + Deflate compression (as per the HTTP-Redirect binding). This tool automatically detects and handles both plain Base64 and Base64+Deflate encoded SAML data.

faqs.q: Is it safe to paste SAML tokens into this decoder?
faqs.a: Yes, completely safe. All decoding happens locally in your browser. Your SAML data is never sent to any server, stored, or logged. The tool runs entirely client-side.

faqs.q: What information is contained in a SAML response?
faqs.a: A SAML response typically contains: the issuer (IdP), a digital signature, status codes, one or more assertions with the subject (NameID), authentication statements, attribute statements (like email, name, roles), and conditions (audience restriction, validity period).

faqs.q: Why is my SAML response failing to decode?
faqs.a: Common causes include: incomplete copy of the Base64 string, URL-encoded characters that need to be decoded first, or the data is not actually SAML. Make sure you copy the entire SAMLResponse value without truncation.

faqs.q: What is XPath and how does it work?
faqs.a: XPath (XML Path Language) is a query language for selecting nodes from XML documents. It uses path-like expressions to navigate the XML tree structure. For example, //book selects all book elements, and //book[@price>30] selects books with a price attribute greater than 30.

faqs.q: What is the difference between XPath and CSS selectors?
faqs.a: XPath can navigate both forward and backward in the XML/HTML tree and supports complex conditions, while CSS selectors only navigate downward. XPath is more powerful for XML querying, while CSS selectors are simpler and faster for HTML styling. XPath supports text content matching; CSS selectors do not.

faqs.q: How do I select elements by attribute in XPath?
faqs.a: Use the @ symbol to select attributes. For example: //div[@class='main'] selects div elements with class 'main', //input[@type='text'] selects text inputs, and //*[@id='header'] selects any element with id 'header'.

faqs.q: What is the difference between / and // in XPath?
faqs.a: A single slash (/) selects from the root or current node's direct children only. Double slash (//) selects matching nodes anywhere in the document regardless of depth. For example, /bookstore/book selects direct children, while //book selects all book elements at any level.

faqs.q: Can I use XPath to query HTML documents?
faqs.a: Yes. XPath works on both XML and well-formed HTML (XHTML). Most browsers support XPath queries via document.evaluate(). This tool accepts any valid XML input, including XHTML documents.

faqs.q: How do I test XPath expressions for Selenium?
faqs.a: Paste your page's HTML source into the XML Input field, then test your XPath locator expressions. This helps you validate selectors before using them in Selenium's find_element(By.XPATH, '...') or Playwright's page.locator('xpath=...') calls.

faqs.q: What XPath functions are supported?
faqs.a: This tool supports standard XPath 1.0 functions including: text(), contains(), starts-with(), string-length(), count(), sum(), position(), last(), not(), and boolean operators (and, or). These work for filtering and matching nodes.

faqs.q: What are Protocol Buffers (protobuf)?
faqs.a: Protocol Buffers is a language-neutral, platform-neutral binary serialization format developed by Google. It's used to serialize structured data for communication between services, data storage, and more. Protobuf is more compact and faster than JSON or XML.

faqs.q: Can I decode protobuf without a .proto schema file?
faqs.a: Yes. This tool performs schema-less decoding by parsing the raw wire format. It identifies field numbers and wire types, and attempts to interpret values as integers, strings, or nested messages. However, without a schema, field names and exact types are unknown.

faqs.q: What is the difference between protobuf and JSON?
faqs.a: Protobuf is a binary format that is smaller (3-10x) and faster to parse than JSON. JSON is human-readable and self-describing. Protobuf requires a schema (.proto file) for proper encoding/decoding, while JSON is schema-optional. Protobuf is preferred for high-performance inter-service communication.

faqs.q: How is protobuf used in gRPC?
faqs.a: gRPC uses protobuf as its default serialization format. Service interfaces and message types are defined in .proto files, which generate client and server code. When gRPC sends data over the network, messages are serialized to protobuf binary format.

faqs.q: What are protobuf wire types?
faqs.a: Protobuf uses wire types to indicate how values are encoded: Varint (0) for integers, 64-bit (1) for fixed64/double, Length-delimited (2) for strings/bytes/nested messages, and 32-bit (5) for fixed32/float. The wire type is encoded alongside the field number in the binary data.

faqs.q: How do I get protobuf data from network traffic?
faqs.a: Use tools like Wireshark, Charles Proxy, or browser DevTools to capture gRPC or HTTP/2 traffic. Extract the protobuf payload bytes and paste them as hex into this decoder. For gRPC-Web traffic, the payload is often Base64-encoded.

faqs.q: Is protobuf binary data safe to paste into this tool?
faqs.a: Yes. All decoding is performed locally in your browser. No data is sent to any server. Your protobuf payloads remain private and are never stored or logged.

faqs.q: What are tokens in AI language models?
faqs.a: Tokens are the basic units that LLMs use to process text. A token can be a word, part of a word, or a punctuation mark. In English, one token is roughly 4 characters or 0.75 words. For example, 'chatbot' is one token, while 'understanding' might be split into 'under' + 'standing'.

faqs.q: How many tokens can GPT-4 and Claude handle?
faqs.a: GPT-4o supports up to 128K tokens context window. Claude 3.5 Sonnet supports 200K tokens. GPT-4 Turbo supports 128K tokens. These limits include both input (prompt) and output (response) tokens combined.

faqs.q: How are AI API costs calculated based on tokens?
faqs.a: AI APIs charge per token, usually priced per 1 million tokens. Input tokens (your prompt) and output tokens (the response) are priced differently, with output tokens typically costing 3-5x more. This tool shows both input and output costs for each model.

faqs.q: Is the token count exact for all models?
faqs.a: The count is an approximation based on the average of ~4 characters per token for English text. Each model uses its own tokenizer (GPT uses tiktoken, Claude uses its own BPE tokenizer), so exact counts may vary slightly. The estimate is accurate enough for cost planning.

faqs.q: How can I reduce token usage to lower API costs?
faqs.a: Remove unnecessary whitespace and verbose instructions. Use concise prompts. Avoid repeating context. Use system messages efficiently. Consider shorter model responses by setting max_tokens. For large documents, use chunking or summarization before sending to the API.

faqs.q: Do different languages use different amounts of tokens?
faqs.a: Yes. English is the most token-efficient language for most LLMs. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and other non-Latin languages typically require 2-3x more tokens per word because the tokenizers were primarily trained on English text. This significantly affects API costs for non-English use.

faqs.q: What is a context window in AI models?
faqs.a: The context window is the maximum number of tokens an AI model can process in a single request, including both the input prompt and the generated output. If your text exceeds the context window, it will be truncated or the API will return an error.

faqs.q: Does this tool send my text to any AI service?
faqs.a: No. Token counting is performed entirely in your browser using a local approximation algorithm. Your text is never sent to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or any other service.

faqs.q: What is a ULID?
faqs.a: A ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) is a 26-character, 128-bit identifier that encodes a timestamp and random data. ULIDs sort naturally by creation time.

faqs.q: ULID vs UUID - which should I use?
faqs.a: Use ULID when you need time-sorted IDs (databases, logs). Use UUID when you need maximum compatibility. ULIDs are URL-safe and more compact than UUIDs.

faqs.q: Are ULIDs truly unique?
faqs.a: Yes. ULIDs combine a 48-bit millisecond timestamp with 80 bits of randomness, making collisions virtually impossible.

faqs.q: Can I extract the timestamp from a ULID?
faqs.a: Yes! The first 10 characters encode the creation timestamp. Use the decode section below the generator to extract it.

faqs.q: What encoding do ULIDs use?
faqs.a: ULIDs use Crockford's Base32 encoding (0-9, A-Z excluding I, L, O, U), which is URL-safe and case-insensitive.

ulid-generator.seoTitle: About ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier)
ulid-generator.seoContent: ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) is a modern alternative to UUID that provides 128-bit unique identifiers with built-in timestamp sorting. Each ULID encodes a millisecond-precision timestamp in the first 48 bits and 80 bits of cryptographic randomness, formatted as a 26-character Crockford Base32 string. This makes ULIDs ideal for database primary keys, distributed systems, and any use case requiring chronologically sortable unique identifiers.

faqs.q: How do I apply the validated unit?

api-rate-limit-calculator.pageDescription: Free API rate limit calculator. Compare costs across GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini and other LLM APIs. Plan usage and estimate monthly bills.
api-rate-limit-calculator.seoTitle: What is API Rate Limit Calculator?
api-rate-limit-calculator.seoContent: API rate limits determine how many requests you can make per minute, hour, or day. This calculator helps you plan API usage, estimate costs across different LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), and check if your usage fits within rate limits.

faqs.q: How are LLM API costs calculated?
faqs.a: LLM APIs charge per token (roughly 4 characters per token). Input tokens and output tokens often have different pricing.

faqs.q: What is RPM?
faqs.a: RPM stands for Requests Per Minute, the maximum number of API calls you can make in a minute. Exceeding this results in 429 rate limit errors.

faqs.q: Are the prices up to date?
faqs.a: Prices shown are approximate as of 2026. Always check the official provider documentation for current rates.

howToUseSteps: Enter your expected daily request volume
Set average input and output token counts
Compare costs across different LLM models
Check if your usage fits within RPM limits

Planning API usage within rate limits

oauth-debugger.name: OAuth 2.0 Debugger
oauth-debugger.description: Debug OAuth 2.0 authorization flows and generate auth URLs
oauth-debugger.pageTitle: OAuth 2.0 Debugger Online – Authorization Flow Tester
oauth-debugger.pageDescription: Free OAuth 2.0 debugger. Build authorization URLs, test PKCE flows, and debug OAuth token exchanges for your applications.
oauth-debugger.seoContent: OAuth 2.0 is the industry standard protocol for authorization. This debugger helps you construct authorization URLs, configure PKCE parameters, and test different OAuth flows (Authorization Code, Implicit, Client Credentials) without writing code.

faqs.q: What is PKCE?
faqs.a: PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) is a security extension for OAuth 2.0 that prevents authorization code interception attacks. Recommended for all public clients.

faqs.q: Which OAuth flow should I use?
faqs.a: Authorization Code + PKCE for web/mobile apps, Client Credentials for machine-to-machine, and avoid Implicit flow (deprecated).

faqs.q: Does this tool actually perform authentication?
faqs.a: This tool builds the authorization URL and parameters. You would then use the generated URL in your browser to start the actual OAuth flow.

howToUseSteps: Select your OAuth flow type
Configure authorization and token endpoints
Enter client ID, redirect URI, and scopes
Copy the generated authorization URL
useCases: Building authorization URLs for different providers

dockerfile-linter.pageTitle: Dockerfile Linter Online – Best Practices & Security Checker
dockerfile-linter.pageDescription: Free Dockerfile linter. Check for best practices, security vulnerabilities, and common mistakes. Get actionable recommendations.
dockerfile-linter.seoContent: A Dockerfile linter analyzes your Docker build instructions for common mistakes, security issues, and deviations from best practices. This tool checks for issues like using :latest tags, running as root, missing HEALTHCHECK, and inefficient layer caching.

faqs.q: What rules does it check?
faqs.a: It checks for pinned base image versions, efficient RUN commands, COPY vs ADD usage, exec form CMD, security concerns, and more.

faqs.q: Is this like Hadolint?
faqs.a: It applies similar best practice rules to Hadolint but runs entirely in your browser with no installation required.

faqs.q: Should I fix all warnings?
faqs.a: Errors should always be fixed. Warnings are recommendations that improve security and performance but may not apply to every situation.

howToUseSteps: Paste your Dockerfile content
Review errors, warnings, and info messages
Fix critical issues first (red), then warnings (yellow)
Re-lint to verify all issues are resolved
useCases: Enforcing best practices in CI/CD pipelines

ssl-certificate-decoder.name: SSL Certificate Decoder
ssl-certificate-decoder.description: Decode and inspect SSL/TLS X.509 certificates
ssl-certificate-decoder.pageTitle: SSL Certificate Decoder Online – X.509 Certificate Inspector
ssl-certificate-decoder.pageDescription: Free SSL certificate decoder. Inspect PEM certificates, check expiry dates, view subject details, and analyze certificate chains.
ssl-certificate-decoder.seoContent: SSL/TLS certificates (X.509) are used to encrypt web traffic and verify server identity. This decoder parses PEM-encoded certificates to show the subject, issuer, validity dates, and other details without using command-line tools.

faqs.q: What certificate formats are supported?
faqs.a: PEM-encoded certificates (Base64 with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- headers) are supported. DER format needs to be converted first.

faqs.q: Can it decode private keys?
faqs.a: It detects private keys and shows their type, but does not expose key material for security reasons.

faqs.q: How do I get my certificate in PEM format?
faqs.a: Use openssl s_client -connect domain:443 to download a site certificate, or check your certificate provider dashboard.

howToUseSteps: Paste your PEM-encoded certificate
View decoded certificate details
Check validity dates and subject information
Review the certificate type and format

font-pairing-tool.seoContent: Font pairing is the art of combining complementary typefaces for headings and body text. Good font pairs create visual hierarchy and readability. faqs.q: How do I choose good font pairs?
faqs.a: Pair a distinctive heading font (serif or display) with a clean body font (sans-serif). Contrast in style while maintaining harmony is key.

faqs.q: Are these Google Fonts free?
faqs.a: Yes, all fonts shown are from Google Fonts and are free for personal and commercial use.

faqs.q: Can I use custom fonts?

helm-chart-validator.seoContent: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes, using Charts to define, install, and manage K8s applications. This validator checks your Chart.yaml for required fields (apiVersion, name, version) and values.yaml for common configuration issues.

faqs.q: What Chart.yaml fields are required?
faqs.a: apiVersion (v2 recommended), name, and version are required. description, type, and appVersion are strongly recommended.

faqs.q: Does it validate templates?
faqs.a: This tool focuses on Chart.yaml and values.yaml validation. Template rendering requires helm template command locally.

faqs.q: What Helm version is supported?
faqs.a: Both Helm v2 (apiVersion: v1) and Helm v3+ (apiVersion: v2) chart formats are validated, with v2 recommended.

Review validation results for both files
Fix any errors before packaging the chart
